The relationship between corpus entities and evidence contracts is illustrated through the process of presenting and accepting new evidence in legal contexts. In the case of Vishal, new evidence was presented by Sandeep Jindal, which led to the judge accepting this evidence and ultimately resulted in Vishal's acquittal [Q6894320::2]. This demonstrates how evidence contracts can influence legal outcomes by allowing new information to be considered in court. 

The evidence does not confirm any specific details about the nature of the evidence contracts themselves or how they are structured, nor does it provide information about other corpus entities related to evidence contracts beyond the example of Vishal.
